title: Unified brand fallback token matrix for directional accents & component overrides
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a deterministic fallback mapping and override rules that let branded color palettes ship safely across light, dark, and high-contrast console themes. Deliverables: a token matrix (primary -> directional accent -> neutral fallback), component-level override guidance for buttons, tables, charts, and badges, Figma token files, a migration checklist for engineering, and automated visual test cases. Acceptance criteria: (1) All brand accents map to a named directional token (accent-1/2/3) for light/dark; (2) Neutral fallbacks maintain 4.5:1 contrast for small text and 3:1 for large UI elements; (3) Component overrides implemented in prototype examples for Button, Table row states, Chart legends, and Badge; (4) Engineering has a clear token-to-CSS-variable mapping and backwards-compatible alias layer to avoid runtime breakage.
comments: 2025-01-28 - Ticket created by Ava: Problem framed — teams keep adding ad-hoc brand colors which break dark-mode contrast and produce inconsistent component states. Proposed approach: a small directional accent system plus neutral fallbacks and component override rules.

2025-01-30 - Design sync: Agreed to make directional accents first-class tokens (accent.positive, accent.warning, accent.brand-1..3). Rafael to prototype Figma token variants for 3 sample brand palettes (partner, enterprise, internal).

2025-02-03 - Prototype uploaded: Figma file "Unified-Fallback-Matrix v0.1" https://figma.com/file/Example/Unified-Fallback-Matrix (internal). Initial mapping showed several brand-1 values failing 4.5:1 at 12px — treat as decorative or move to brand-3 neutralized token.

2025-02-06 - Accessibility review: UX researcher Kim Patel ran contrast checks and recommended an algorithmic step: if brand accent < 4.5:1 on target background, auto-fallback to neutral-accent-1 and mark as 'decorative' in token metadata. Rafael to add metadata flags in Figma tokens.

2025-02-10 - Engineering feasibility: Frontend lead Mei Huang confirmed ability to implement alias layer (--rwd-accent-brand-1 -> --rwd-accent-directional-2 or --rwd-neutral-600) and requested explicit CSS var names and usage examples for Button, Table, Chart legend. Also called out performance constraints for chart palette swapping (avoid re-creating canvas styles on every theme switch).

2025-02-12 - Design decision: Use three-tier fallback strategy: (1) directionally mapped accent token (theme-aware), (2) neutral fallback token if contrast fails, (3) decorative flag for small non-critical UI. Documented mapping table in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Design/Unified+Brand+Fallbacks.

2025-02-15 - PRD comment from PM Lara Singh: Please add migration notes for Dedicated and Private consoles where customers supply their own brand tokens. Proposed workflow: import brand palette -> run token analyzer -> produce suggested mapping + human review step.

2025-02-17 - Visual QA plan: Create per-component golden screenshots for three brands x 2 themes x 4 viewport sizes. Add automated Percy snapshots and a manual checklist for edge cases (badly saturated logos, gradients). Rafael started the Figma-to-screenshot pipeline task.

2025-02-18 - Blocker noted by Engineering: legacy token aliases (rwd-legacy-primary) used by several micro-frontends; need a compatibility shim for two sprints. Added dependency ENG-19876 to tech backlog.

Next steps: finalize token matrix v0.2 in Figma, export JSON tokens, handoff to engineering with mapping doc and example overrides, add unit/visual tests, and schedule design review with Platform PM on 2025-02-24.
